output.brief: The rise in Corvane's mishandled bags is very unlikely to be mainly a Tessaly handling failure. On 1 September Corvane also switched its bag-tag stock. Tags on the new Fennick stock fail automatic reading about 11.8% of the time, against 1.5% before. Corvane transfer tags and Pelion tags stay near 1.4%. Those bags are diverted to the manual encode desk, where waits roughly quadrupled, and 91% of the encode-path bags that missed their flight reached the lateral after it had closed. Pelion, handled by the same Tessaly crews, shows no rise. On 14–16 October, counters using old Brackwater stock from stores failed at 1.6% while kiosks on Fennick stock failed at 12.1% on the same days. I'm not sure whether the stock itself is defective or whether the printers need a different heat setting. Do not issue the breach notice or withhold the fee. Switch counters and kiosks back to Brackwater stock now, since about five weeks are in stores. Then test Fennick against the printer settings, and hold any claim against Fennick until that is known. Asking HBAA for an extra encode workstation in the evening bank is a reasonable temporary measure.
